newsitem.title: spain: Spain employers, unions reiterate desire for pact.
newsitem.headline: Spain employers, unions reiterate desire for pact.

text.p: Spain's employers and unions reiterated on Wednesday their desire to reach an accord on labour reforms and said advances had already been made in talks.
"The areas where we are coming closer to an accord are giving us hope that a deal will be reached," Juan Jimenez, Secretary General for employers association CEOE, told reporters.
Employers earlier relaxed their demands and abandoned proposals for lower severance pay -- a key sticking point in the talks so far.
Talks are now centring on labour contracts, in particular those for youths who suffer most from unemployment in Spain, unions said.
Employers and unions resumed talks on Wednesday after a marathon session on Tuesday that ended in no deal. Unions could not rule out the possibility that talks may continue on Thursday.
Fernando Puig, representative for the Workers' Commissions union (CCOO), said talks were advancing, albeit slowly, and both sides were trying their hardest to reach a "coherent and balanced" accord.
Toni Ferrer, representative for the General Workers' union (UGT) said the talks were being conducted in a positive climate, but said a precise time for reaching an accord had not yet been mentioned.
Talks broke for lunch at midday, and are due to restart at 1500 GMT.
